page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Overtime
title: Overtime
description:
Someone's been working very long hours at Tip Top Trading. Anna is burning the candle at both ends – in other words she’s working from early until late preparing for the launch of their latest product – the Imperial Lemon. Denise is concerned about her working overtime, something she would never consider doing. But will Anna's extra efforts pay off or will she end up selling bananas instead of lemons?
This episode explores language that describes working overtime or working long hours.
phrases: Burning the candle at both ends.

listening_challenge.question: What phrase does Denise use to mean Anna will be no use to anyone?
listening_challenge.answer:
Denise use to mean Anna will be no use to anyone? 
As useful as a chocolate teapot

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: It's late at the offices of Tip Top Trading. Anna is alone, working. Again. She's been doing this all week, she wants her presentation to Mr Lime to be perfect so she's been spending hours and hours on it. Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Don't interrupt! I'm busy.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Woah!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sorry.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna, you're really burning the candle at both ends.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Burning the candle at both ends – it means working very hard – working late and getting up early to work all the time.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh. I didn't know that expression.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Well here are some more: 
You're doing overtime; which means you're working longer than office hours. 
You're putting in the hours; which means you are spending all the time needed to achieve something.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, I'm putting in the hours to make sure my presentation is perfect.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: And if you don't mind me saying so, you might burn out; which means you are working so hard that you might get very tired and run out of energy.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm not burning out. I'm full of energy. I just need to finish this bit...

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: My goodness, nothing's locked. Do you think we've been burgled?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh no! I left my lap-book and my me-pad on the desk... and my i-top – they're worth thousands! They're all the latest versions!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I left out my elephant mug and my lady-curve nail file. They better not have stolen them!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: (Talking in her sleep) but it's premium, premium, faux-orange premium!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: It's Anna, she's asleep. Anna!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: (waking up with a jump) Oh! Lemons! Denise? Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Have you spent the night asleep at your desk Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Is it morning? Oh dear, yes I think so.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well, at least we haven't been burgled then.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna, you've really been burning the candle at both ends lately.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes, you've been doing hours and hours of overtime. Most people get their work done within office hours and anyway, we don't pay overtime here. You’ll never find me working late!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes, I'd noticed that Denise.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But this presentation must be perfect.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: If you're not careful, you'll burn out! Then you'll really be of no use to anyone. You'll be as useful as a chocolate teapot.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It's good that you're putting in the hours Anna, but you should calm down. Look at me, I do very successful presentations without spending hours preparing.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Ha!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: In my presentation to Every Apple I just swooshed in with no preparation after a night on the town. I charmed them. They loved me!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Idiot. I bet he actually spent hours preparing he just can't admit it.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, maybe you're right. I can't think clearly anymore, I'm so tired. I need to sleep properly otherwise I'll end up trying to sell bananas instead of lemons.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna has finally got the message: she's realised she's been working too much. She needs to be realistic. Here's a reminder of some of the phrases we heard to talk about how much Anna had been working:
Let's hope she's thinking clearly by the time she has to do her presentation. Join us next time to find out! Bye.
